label: Friends turned ideological rivals
summary: The founding conflict of the X-Men. They met as young men in Israel (shown in flashback in Uncanny X-Men #161, 1982), bonded over being mutants, and split over whether coexistence with humans was possible. Every subsequent decade restages the argument; the Krakoan era finally put them on the same council.

events.note: Magneto attacks Cape Citadel; the X-Men's first mission is against Xavier's old friend.
Flashback: Charles and Erik meet in Haifa, fight Baron Strucker together, and part over ideology.
Xavier, dying, hands Magneto the school and the New Mutants.
Fatal Attractions prelude; Magneto returns to Asteroid M and dies (apparently) in the fall.
Xavier and Magneto co-found the mutant nation of Krakoa.

label: First love, marriage, Phoenix, death
summary: The franchise's central romance. A shy mutual crush in 1963 became the marriage in X-Men #30 (1994), was broken by Jean's death as Dark Phoenix, by her resurrection, by Scott's psychic affair with Emma Frost, and by Jean's second death. Her Krakoan return left them cordial co-workers rather than a couple.

events.note: Scott's unspoken feelings for Jean are established in the first issue.
Dark Phoenix Saga ends with Jean's suicide on the Moon to stop herself.
Scott and Jean marry.
Jean discovers Scott's psychic affair with Emma.
Jean is killed by Xorn/Magneto; she tells Scott to live.

label: Rivals for Jean, then for the X-Men
summary: Started as a love-triangle rivalry over Jean Grey and became a philosophical one: Logan, the soldier, came to believe children should be kept out of the war; Scott, the field leader, came to believe there was no one else to fight it. The 2011 Schism split the X-Men between them.

events.note: Logan joins; friction with Cyclops's leadership is immediate.
Wolverine's famous 'Now it's my turn' in the Hellfire Club, while Scott is captured.
The two fight on Utopia over whether to send students into battle; Wolverine leaves to reopen the school.
Logan sides with the Avengers against a Phoenix-possessed Cyclops.

label: Unrequited, mostly
summary: Logan's attraction to Jean is written as intense and almost never acted on; Jean's response varies by writer from fond refusal to genuine temptation. The relationship is largely about restraint, and it is consummated only in alternate futures.

events.note: Logan's interest in Jean is first made explicit.
Stranded on Asteroid M, Jean and Logan kiss; Logan kills her so the Phoenix will take over and save them.
Phoenix-Jean seeks out Logan; he refuses her repeatedly.

label: Psychic affair to power couple
summary: Began as telepathic 'therapy' during Scott's marriage, became an affair, and after Jean's death became the X-Men's leadership couple through the Utopia era. Ended when Phoenix-possessed Scott turned on Emma; they have remained allies with history since.

events.note: Emma offers Scott telepathic counselling; it turns intimate.
Jean, from the future, pushes Scott toward Emma; they kiss on Jean's grave and reopen the school.
Headmaster and headmistress; the relationship becomes the team's centre.
Scott takes Emma's share of the Phoenix by force.

label: Rivals who respect each other
summary: A rivalry with uncommon mutual respect. Jean's psychic confrontation with Emma in New X-Men #139 is the high point; by the Krakoan era they are colleagues who occasionally still needle each other about Scott.

events.note: Jean tears through Emma's mind after discovering the affair.

events.issue: Phoenix Resurrection: The Return of Jean Grey #5 (2018)
events.note: Jean's return; Emma among those present.

label: Closest confidants, briefly lovers
summary: The two most senior members of the 1975 team, each the other's most trusted colleague. Written as a near-sibling friendship for decades, with a romantic period during Jason Aaron's Wolverine and the X-Men (2012–2014) that the line has mostly treated as a chapter rather than a change.

events.note: Storm takes over as team leader with Logan's backing.
Storm and Logan begin a relationship.
Logan dies; Storm leads the mourning.

label: Big sister, then peer
summary: Storm was the first adult X-Man Kitty bonded with; the relationship strained when Storm's punk-era change (Uncanny X-Men #173) frightened her, and matured into equals by the time Kitty led the team.

events.note: Storm recruits Kitty in Deerfield, Illinois.
Kitty rejects Storm's new look and the two fall out.
Reconciliation.

label: Decades on and off
summary: A teenage crush that became a long, intermittently written romance. Broken off in Secret Wars (1985) when Piotr fell for an alien healer; revived in Astonishing X-Men; nearly ended in marriage in X-Men Gold #30 (2018), when Kitty called it off at the altar.

events.note: Kitty, 13, is immediately smitten with Piotr.
Piotr falls for Zsaji on Battleworld; the relationship ends.
Colossus returns from apparent death; the romance restarts.
Kitty halts the wedding; Rogue and Gambit marry instead.

label: Brother and sister
summary: Piotr's protectiveness and Illyana's transformation into a demon sorceress define the relationship; he keeps trying to see the child she was, and she keeps refusing to be seen that way. Her death in the Legacy Virus storyline (Uncanny X-Men #303, 1993) and later return is one of his central griefs.

events.note: Illyana is taken to Limbo and returns moments later aged seven years.
Illyana dies of the Legacy Virus.
Magik, restored, rejoins the team.

label: From fear to family
summary: Kitty initially recoiled from Kurt's appearance; Claremont used her growing affection for him as the story of the reader learning to see past surfaces. They are close for the rest of the run.

events.note: Kitty is frightened by Nightcrawler on first meeting.
Christmas issue: Kitty alone at the mansion, Kurt among those she now counts as family.

label: Best friends; the devil and the saint
summary: The franchise's most consistently written male friendship. Kurt is the one person Logan does not perform for; Kurt's death in X-Force vol. 3 #26 (2010) broke Logan, and his return on Krakoa restored the pairing.

events.note: Early baseball-game issue establishing the team's off-duty bonds.
Nightcrawler dies saving Hope Summers; Logan carries the grief for years.
Kurt returns from the afterlife.

label: Mother who abandoned him
summary: Hinted at since Uncanny X-Men #142 (1981) and confirmed in 1994: Mystique bore Kurt and, fleeing a mob, let him fall into a river. The relationship is about whether he can forgive her and whether she wants him to. Krakoa, where she sat on the Quiet Council while he served as its moral voice, kept the question open.

events.note: Mystique hints she knows Nightcrawler's parentage.
Mystique confirms she is Kurt's mother.
'The Draco' names Azazel as his father.

label: Foster mother and daughter
summary: Mystique and Destiny raised Rogue after her powers manifested, then used her as a Brotherhood weapon. Rogue's defection to the X-Men was a betrayal from Mystique's side and an escape from Rogue's; the two have spent decades alternating between manipulation and genuine care.

events.note: Rogue debuts as Mystique's protégé, absorbing Ms. Marvel's powers permanently.
Rogue asks Xavier for help and joins the X-Men.
Rogue gains control of her power; Mystique's manipulations in the surrounding arc resurface.

label: The 90s' great slow burn
summary: A romance built on Rogue being unable to touch anyone and Gambit being unable to be honest with anyone. Spanned betrayals (his Marauders past, the Antarctica abandonment in Uncanny X-Men #350), separations, and the 2018 wedding; still married on Krakoa and after.

events.note: Their flirtation begins in earnest.
Rogue abandons Gambit in Antarctica after his Mutant Massacre role is revealed.
Rogue and Gambit marry.

label: Savage Land interlude
summary: A brief, deliberate romance in the Savage Land that Claremont wrote as two outsiders recognising each other. It mattered mostly for what it set up: Rogue's enduring sympathy for Magneto and the alternate-universe marriage in the Age of Apocalypse.

events.note: Rogue and Magneto, depowered and stranded, become close.
Magneto executes Zaladane; Rogue cannot follow him.

label: Married, with a son
summary: In the Age of Apocalypse, where Xavier died before founding the X-Men, Magneto leads the team and is married to Rogue; their son is Charles. The pairing is the clearest example of the database's premise: the same two characters, a different continuity, a different relationship.

events.note: Magneto and Rogue shown as husband and wife.

label: Favourite son to patricide
summary: Xavier's first and most loyal student. The relationship curdled as Scott learned how much Xavier had hidden (Deadly Genesis, 2006), and ended when a Phoenix-possessed Scott killed Xavier. Krakoa, with Xavier resurrected, treated it as a wound neither wanted to discuss.

events.note: Scott is Xavier's field leader from the first mission.
Scott learns Xavier erased his memory of a lost team and expels him from the mansion.
Dark Phoenix Cyclops kills Xavier.

label: Mentor, with a buried complication
summary: Xavier trained Jean's telepathy from childhood. X-Men #3 (1964) briefly gave him secret romantic feelings for her, a thread later writers abandoned and then treated as evidence of his ethical blind spots.

events.note: A thought balloon reveals Xavier's attraction to Jean; it is never pursued.
Jean's Phoenix return; Xavier's role in suppressing her power earlier is part of the backstory.

label: Teacher, then colleague
summary: Logan trained Kitty in Japan after her kidnapping by Ogun; she is the first of his series of young protégées (later Jubilee, Armor, Laura). As an adult she ran his school after his death.

events.note: Logan rescues and retrains Kitty in Japan; she takes the name Shadowcat.
Kitty is co-headmistress of the Jean Grey School.

label: Mutual contempt, grudging respect
summary: Kitty never forgave Emma's Hellfire Club past; Whedon's Astonishing X-Men built the team's internal tension on Kitty's suspicion that Emma had not changed. Emma's later rescue of Kitty from the bullet (Uncanny X-Men #522, 2010) did not fully close the account.

events.note: Kitty is recruited specifically to keep an eye on Emma.
Emma, under the Hellfire Club's influence, turns on Kitty.

label: Lifelong partners
summary: Claremont wrote them as a couple from Destiny's first appearance, in code, because editorial would not allow it to be stated. Destiny's death in Uncanny X-Men #255 (1990) drove Mystique's choices for decades; her Krakoan resurrection, which Mystique forced, is the spine of Inferno (2021) and Immortal X-Men.

events.note: Destiny debuts with the Brotherhood alongside Mystique.
Destiny is killed by Legion.
Destiny is resurrected; the two are stated on the page as married.

label: Oldest friends in the franchise
summary: The two original X-Men who most often left and returned together (the Champions, the Defenders, X-Factor). Bobby came out to Hank in All-New X-Men #40 (2015) among the first to know; the Krakoan era's divergence, with Hank running X-Force's dirty work, strained but did not break it.

events.note: Both among the original five.
Both leave the X-Men to form the Champions.
Young Bobby comes out; adult Bobby follows in Uncanny X-Men #600.

label: Brothers, perpetually compared
summary: Separated as children after a plane crash, reunited as adults. Alex has spent most of his career defining himself against Scott—leading X-Factor and the Avengers Unity Squad as the brother who is not Cyclops—and the two have fought on opposite sides more than once.

events.note: Alex is introduced and revealed as Scott's brother.
Alex leads the Unity Squad while Scott is imprisoned.

label: The team's two matriarchs
summary: Close from the start of the new team; Storm was Jean's closest female friend through the Phoenix years and held the team together in her absences.

events.note: Jean becomes Phoenix; Storm is at her side.
Returned Jean recruits Storm first for her new team.

label: Teenage version
summary: In the Ultimate universe they are teenagers, the romance is more volatile, and Jean briefly chooses Wolverine. Included as a continuity contrast to the 616 marriage.

events.note: Scott and Jean established as a couple at Xavier's.
Jean leaves Scott for Logan, briefly.

label: Student who became the professor's peer
summary: Hank was the original X-Man most like Xavier intellectually, and the one who most often argued with him as an equal. On Krakoa their relationship inverted: Beast ran the operations Xavier would not look at directly.

events.note: Among the original five students.
Beast takes charge of Krakoa's intelligence arm with Xavier's tacit blessing.

label: The youngest student
summary: Bobby was the youngest of the first class and the one Xavier treated most as a child; later writers used that to explain how long it took anyone to notice the scale of his power.

events.note: Joins as the youngest of the original five.

label: Original teammates, later at odds
summary: Teammates for sixty years whose friendship cracked when Hank refused to follow Scott into militancy on Utopia (Uncanny X-Men #519–520, 2010) and then brought the time-displaced original X-Men to the present to shame him (All-New X-Men #1, 2012).

events.note: Original teammates.
Beast pulls the young X-Men from the past to confront the adult Cyclops.

label: The leader and the class clown
summary: Bobby spent the Silver Age needling Scott's seriousness and the modern era following him anyway; he was on Scott's side of the Schism.

events.note: Original teammates.
Iceman stays with Cyclops on Utopia.

label: Closest of the original five
summary: Hank and Jean were the two originals who stayed closest; he was the scientist she trusted with the Phoenix question, and her deaths hit him hardest after Scott's.

events.note: Reunited in X-Factor after Jean's return.

label: Teammates; she outed him before he did
summary: The time-displaced young Jean read Bobby's mind and told him he was gay in All-New X-Men #40 (2015), a scene that was criticised for her lack of consent and celebrated for what it did for the character.

events.note: Young Jean tells young Bobby what she has read in his mind.

label: The scientist and the soldier
summary: Rarely hostile, often sharp: two of the team's most senior members who disagree about means. Their Krakoan-era X-Force partnership, in which Beast became the more ruthless of the two, inverted the dynamic.

events.note: Both on Krakoa's X-Force; Beast's ethics drift past Wolverine's.

label: The marriage Marvel undid
summary: 'Face it, tiger, you just hit the jackpot.' From that first line to the wedding in Amazing Spider-Man Annual #21 (1987) to the deal with Mephisto in One More Day (2007) that erased the marriage from everyone's memory. They have been on and off ever since; the relationship is the clearest example of editorial intervening in a dynamic.

events.note: MJ's face is finally shown.
MJ reveals she has always known Peter is Spider-Man.
The wedding.
One More Day: the marriage is erased.

label: First love, ended on a bridge
summary: Peter's college girlfriend and the great tragedy of the book. Her death at the Green Goblin's hands — with Peter's own web-line possibly snapping her neck — is the moment the series stopped being a Silver Age comic.

events.note: Gwen introduced at Empire State University.
The Night Gwen Stacy Died.

label: Best friend who became the Goblin
summary: Roommates at ESU; Harry's drug addiction (ASM #96–98, the issues that broke the Comics Code), his discovery of Peter's identity, and his turn as the second Green Goblin. He died saving Peter in Spectacular Spider-Man #200 (1993) and was later restored by One More Day.

events.note: Harry's drug storyline, published without Code approval.
Harry becomes the Green Goblin.
Harry dies saving Peter and Normie.

label: Archenemy who knows his name
summary: The only Spider-Man villain whose enmity is fully personal: Norman learned Peter's identity in ASM #39 (1966), killed Gwen in #121, apparently died in #122, and returned in 1996 to orchestrate the Clone Saga. Every major Spider-Man storyline about loss runs through him.

events.note: Osborn unmasked as the Goblin; learns Peter's identity.
Goblin impaled on his own glider.
Norman revealed alive, behind the Clone Saga.

label: Son who could never satisfy him
summary: Norman's contempt for Harry is the origin of nearly everything wrong with Harry; the Goblin identity passed from father to son as a kind of inheritance.

events.note: Norman's origin reveals his coldness toward Harry.

label: The reason for the mask
summary: For four decades the book's central secret existed to protect her. When she finally learned the truth — Amazing Spider-Man vol. 2 #38 (2002), in a single conversation — it was one of the best-regarded issues of the era.

events.note: Uncle Ben dies; May becomes Peter's responsibility.
'The Conversation': May tells Peter she knows.

label: She wanted Spider-Man, not Peter
summary: Felicia fell for the mask and was openly disappointed by the man under it — the inverse of the MJ relationship. Partners, lovers and occasional opponents for forty years; the pairing was written as adults, which made it unusual for the book.

events.note: Black Cat debuts.
Peter unmasks; Felicia is unimpressed by Peter Parker.

label: The rejected suit and the ruined man
summary: Eddie Brock blamed Spider-Man for his career; the symbiote blamed him for rejection. Together they were the first villain who knew Peter's identity and could evade his spider-sense. The enmity has softened since Venom became an anti-hero.

events.note: Venom debuts, menacing Mary Jane.
Truce: Venom becomes an anti-hero.

label: Rival who lived in his body
summary: Otto was the first villain to beat Spider-Man and, fifty years later, the one who replaced him: dying, he swapped minds with Peter and ran as the Superior Spider-Man for thirty-one issues. No other rivalry at Marvel has that shape.

events.note: Doc Ock defeats Spider-Man in his first appearance.
Otto takes over Peter's body.
Otto yields the body back to Peter.

label: Two Spider-Men
summary: Peter first met Miles across universes in Spider-Men (2012); after Secret Wars moved Miles to 616 they shared New York, and Peter became the mentor he never had.

events.note: Peter crosses into the Ultimate universe and meets Miles.
Miles operating in Earth-616.

label: Successor to a dead Peter
summary: In the Ultimate universe Miles took the name after Peter Parker died (Ultimate Spider-Man #160); the two met only briefly when a resurrected Ultimate Peter returned. A different relationship from the 616 one: inheritance, not mentorship.

events.note: Ultimate Peter Parker dies.
Miles debuts.

label: Rivals written as friends
summary: Introduced as competing love interests, they were mostly friends on the page; MJ's silent presence at Peter's apartment after Gwen's death (ASM #122) is the panel that turned her from party girl into the series' adult.

events.note: MJ stays with Peter the night after Gwen dies.

label: Avengers teammates who annoy each other
summary: A 1987 one-shot in which Logan's world got a civilian killed set the tone; New Avengers (2005–2012) made them teammates and the odd-couple friendship became one of Bendis's recurring jokes.

events.note: Peter accidentally kills Logan's old flame Charlie.
Both founding members of the New Avengers.

label: Ultimate universe teenage romance
summary: In the Ultimate universe, Peter and Kitty dated briefly between his breakups with MJ — a pairing with no 616 equivalent, and a good example of what a continuity filter is for.

events.note: Peter and Kitty begin dating.
Kitty ends it; Peter returns to MJ.

label: Friends who went to war with each other
summary: The Avengers' two leaders: the soldier who distrusts systems and the engineer who builds them. Civil War (2006–07) split the superhero community between them, and Steve's assassination at the end of it is the thing Tony has never stopped apologising for.

events.note: Stark's Avengers find Rogers frozen in ice.
Registration splits them; Cap surrenders in #7.
Steve is shot on the courthouse steps.
Rebuilt partnership at the head of a larger Avengers.

label: The partner who came back
summary: Bucky was Cap's kid sidekick in the war, dead for sixty years of publishing, then revealed in 2005 as the brainwashed Winter Soldier. Steve's refusal to give up on him, and Bucky carrying the shield after Steve's death, is Brubaker's whole run.

events.note: Cap's survivor's guilt over Bucky's death established.
The Winter Soldier is revealed as Bucky.
Bucky becomes Captain America.

label: Founding scientists
summary: Two founding Avengers and the team's engineers; Tony's later disdain for Hank (over Ultron, over Jan) and Hank's resentment of Tony's success colour a relationship that is cordial on the surface.

events.note: Both founding members.
Pym merges with Ultron; Stark among those who must respond.

label: Marriage ended by a blow
summary: Partners from Jan's first appearance, married in Avengers #60 (1969), divorced after Hank struck her during his Yellowjacket breakdown in Avengers #213 (1981). Marvel has never let either character forget it, and neither should it.

events.note: Wedding (with Hank as Yellowjacket).
Hank hits Jan; the marriage ends.
Jan, now leader, keeps Hank off the team.

label: Creator and creation
summary: Hank built Ultron from his own brain patterns and Ultron has spent sixty years trying to kill 'father'. The relationship is written explicitly as Oedipal, and it ended — for a while — with the two merged into one being (Rage of Ultron, 2015).

events.note: Ultron's origin as Pym's creation revealed.
Pym and Ultron fused.

label: Built to be a weapon, chose not to be
summary: Ultron created the Vision to infiltrate the Avengers; the Vision defected in his first issue. Ultron's resentment of his 'son' and the Vision's refusal to be defined by his maker mirror the Pym–Ultron relationship one generation down.

events.note: Vision created by Ultron, joins the Avengers.

label: The witch and the machine
summary: Married in Giant-Size Avengers #4 (1975), had twin sons by magic, lost them when they were revealed as fragments of Mephisto (Avengers West Coast #52, 1989). The grief drove Avengers Disassembled and House of M; the marriage never recovered.

events.note: Wedding.
The twins are unmade.
Disassembled: Wanda destroys the team and the Vision.
Working together again, uneasily.

label: Twins
summary: Introduced together in Magneto's Brotherhood and inseparable since; Pietro's protectiveness and Wanda's instability are the relationship's two constants. Both left the Brotherhood for the Avengers in Avengers #16 (1965).

events.note: Debut in the Brotherhood of Evil Mutants.
Both join the Avengers.
Pietro manipulates a broken Wanda into remaking reality.

label: Father, then not
summary: Revealed as Wanda and Pietro's father in 1983, retconned out in AXIS/Uncanny Avengers (2014–15). For thirty years the relationship was the point where the X-Men and Avengers overlapped; Magneto's grief at the retcon was written as real.

events.note: Magneto learns he is their father.
Magneto nearly kills Pietro over the House of M.
The parentage is undone.

label: The son who could never please him
summary: Pietro inherited Magneto's arrogance without his conviction; their relationship was one of mutual disappointment until the retcon.

events.note: Magneto beats Pietro nearly to death for using Wanda.

label: Brothers, forever
summary: Adopted brothers whose rivalry is the oldest continuously published relationship at Marvel after the FF's. Loki's schemes assembled the Avengers; his death and rebirth as a child (Siege, 2010) and Thor's refusal to give up on him are the modern version of the story.

events.note: Loki debuts, already scheming.
Loki's plot against Thor accidentally forms the Avengers.
Loki dies saving Asgard.
Reborn as Kid Loki.

label: Who's stronger
summary: The Marvel universe's longest-running strength contest, written as a friendship with a grudge. Planet Hulk/World War Hulk (2006–07) made it serious.

events.note: 'The Mighty Thor Battles the Incredible Hulk!'
Hulk returns to Earth for revenge on the Illuminati.

label: The man who shot him into space
summary: Founding Avengers, but Tony's Illuminati exiled Bruce to another planet (Planet Hulk, 2006) and Hulk came back to break them. The relationship is the clearest example of Stark deciding for everyone.

events.note: Both founding members.
Illuminati launch the Hulk into space.
Hulk destroys Stark's armour and Avengers Tower.

label: She recruited him; he reformed for her
summary: Natasha, still a Soviet agent, seduced Clint into attacking Iron Man; he joined the Avengers to go straight and she followed later. Written as a short romance and a permanent friendship.

events.note: Hawkeye debuts as Black Widow's partner in crime.
Clint joins the Avengers.

label: Partners in San Francisco
summary: Natasha and Matt were a couple and co-headliners (the book was retitled Daredevil and the Black Widow) through the early 1970s. One of the few Daredevil romances to end without a funeral.

events.note: Natasha joins the book.
The relationship ends.

label: Trained together in the Red Room
summary: Brubaker revealed that the Winter Soldier had trained Natasha in the Red Room and that they had been lovers; they resumed it after Bucky's return and it ended when her memory of him was erased.

events.note: Bucky and Natasha's shared past revealed.
Natasha's memories of Bucky are erased; the relationship ends.

label: The loudmouth and the leader
summary: Clint spent the Silver Age mouthing off to Cap and the Bronze Age wanting his approval; the relationship is affectionate competition, and Clint has led teams specifically to prove the point.

events.note: 'The Old Order Changeth': Clint joins under Cap's leadership.
Clint leads his own team.

label: The captain and the reformed villain
summary: Steve took in the Maximoff twins from Magneto's Brotherhood; for decades he was the Avenger Wanda trusted most, which is why her turning on the team in Disassembled hurt.

events.note: Cap recruits Wanda and Pietro.

label: Allies who went to war in Civil War II
summary: Both recovering alcoholics, both Avengers leaders; Civil War II (2016) put them on opposite sides over predictive justice and ended with Tony in a coma.

events.note: Carol's precog policing vs. Tony's objection; Tony nearly dies.

label: She stole her life
summary: Rogue permanently absorbed Carol's powers and memories in 1981; Carol spent years rebuilding herself as Binary. They have since been teammates, but the relationship is Rogue's original sin.

events.note: Rogue drains Ms. Marvel on the Golden Gate Bridge.
The Carol persona inside Rogue is separated from her.
Working together; the history is acknowledged.

label: King and queen of Wakanda
summary: Met as teenagers (retconned in 1980), married in Black Panther vol. 4 #18 (2006) in a wedding that was a Civil War event, annulled when Storm stood with the Phoenix Five against Wakanda in AvX.

events.note: Their teenage meeting in Africa shown.
Wedding.
T'Challa annuls the marriage.

label: Wartime friends
summary: T'Challa's father fought beside Cap in the war (Flags of Our Fathers, 2010); T'Challa himself joined the Avengers at Cap's invitation and has been the team member most willing to tell Steve no.

events.note: T'Challa joins the Avengers.

label: Wolverine's first fight
summary: Logan debuted fighting the Hulk and the two have been rematching since; Old Man Logan (2008) imagined a future where the Hulk's descendants killed Logan's family.

events.note: Wolverine's first appearance.
Old Man Logan.

label: Marvel's first marriage
summary: Engaged from the first issue, married in Fantastic Four Annual #3 (1965), parents of Franklin and Valeria. The marriage has survived Reed's neglect, Namor's attentions, Sue's turn as Malice and a Civil War separation; it is the model every other Marvel marriage is measured against.

events.note: The wedding, crashed by every villain in the book.
Franklin is born.
Sue leaves Reed over his support for registration.

label: College rivals, forever
summary: Doom blames Reed for the lab accident that scarred his face; Reed knows it was Doom's own arrogance. Sixty years of the two smartest men alive refusing to concede. Doom briefly joined the Avengers (2015) and Reed rebuilt the multiverse after Secret Wars — with Doom's face healed, as a gift Doom never asked for.

events.note: Doom debuts.
Origin: the accident at Empire State.
Reed takes Doom's power and heals his face.

label: The one person he's courteous to
summary: Doom's respect for Sue is a running thread — he delivered Valeria (Fantastic Four vol. 3 #54, 2002) and named her — and Sue is the one FF member who has occasionally trusted him.

events.note: Doom delivers Valeria and becomes her godfather.

label: The suitor who never stopped
summary: Namor has pursued Sue since his 1962 revival; she has been tempted exactly often enough to keep the thread alive. Marvel's longest-running unrequited romance.

events.note: Namor revived; attracted to Sue immediately.
Namor kidnaps Sue; Reed fights for her.

label: Big sister
summary: Sue raised Johnny after their mother's death; she is the only authority he has ever accepted. His death in Fantastic Four #587 (2011) and return were written through her.

events.note: Johnny dies in the Negative Zone.
Johnny returns.

label: Pranks and loyalty
summary: Johnny's practical jokes on Ben are the FF's longest-running comedy and its best proof of family. Johnny's death left Ben the hole in his life the book had been setting up for fifty years.

events.note: The first prank.
Ben's grief after Johnny's death.

label: The friend he turned to stone
summary: Reed's college roommate and pilot, who flew the rocket out of loyalty and paid for it. Ben's periodic rage at Reed, and his deeper refusal to leave him, is the Fantastic Four's emotional spine.

events.note: The flight.
'This Man, This Monster': a stranger's sacrifice restores Reed and Ben's bond.

label: Jealousy to friendship
summary: Ben's first encounter with the Surfer was a jealous brawl over Alicia Masters; it became one of the Surfer's few Earth friendships.

events.note: Ben attacks the Surfer over Alicia.
The Surfer, freed from exile, remains close to Ben and Alicia.

label: Herald and master
summary: Norrin Radd offered himself as herald to spare his planet; Galactus took his memories so he could serve without conscience. The Surfer's rebellion on Earth and his exile are the Galactus Trilogy. Later a reconciliation, and later still a rescue.

events.note: The Galactus Trilogy.
Galactus lifts the exile.

label: The rivalry that became family
summary: Peter tried to join the FF for money in his first issue and fought Johnny repeatedly after; by the 1970s they were best friends, and Johnny's will named Peter his replacement on the team (FF #1, 2011).

events.note: Spider-Man crashes the Baxter Building.
First Torch/Spider-Man team-up.
Peter joins the Future Foundation in Johnny's place.

label: The scientist who finally noticed him
summary: Reed treated Peter as a nuisance for decades and as a peer after Civil War; Spider-Man's time with the Future Foundation was the first time a Marvel adult took Peter Parker's mind seriously.

events.note: Reed invites Peter into the Future Foundation.

label: Invaders
summary: Namor and Cap fought the war together as Invaders (retroactively, 1975) and it was Namor's tantrum that thawed Cap in Avengers #4. Allies who do not like each other.

events.note: Namor hurls Cap's frozen body into the current.
Wartime team-ups established.

label: Villains who keep teaming up
summary: The FF's two great antagonists have allied against them every decade since 1962 and betrayed each other each time.

events.note: Doom and Namor's first alliance.
Namor in Doom's Cabal.

label: Gods who don't share
summary: Doom, as God Emperor of Battleworld, killed Thanos with a flick in Secret Wars #8 (2016) — the most casual death in a Thanos story.

events.note: Doom tears out Thanos's skeleton.

label: The love he can't save
summary: College lovers; she became an assassin, he became a vigilante; she died in his arms in Daredevil #181 (1982). Her resurrection has never quite reunited them.

events.note: Elektra debuts; the college romance revealed.
Bullseye kills Elektra.
Elektra resurrected and sent away.

label: Mutual destruction
summary: Miller gave Daredevil the Kingpin and the two have been destroying each other's lives since: Fisk learned Matt's identity in Born Again (1986) and burned his life down; Matt has had him imprisoned, exiled and deposed as mayor.

events.note: Kingpin enters the book.
Born Again.
Fisk's mayoralty ends in war with Daredevil.

label: The villain Daredevil stole
summary: Fisk was a Spider-Man villain for fourteen years before Miller moved him to Hell's Kitchen; the two books still fight over him. Fisk's shooting of Aunt May (Back in Black, 2007) brought him back into Peter's story.

events.note: Kingpin debuts.
Peter beats Fisk nearly to death in prison.

label: Neighbours who know each other's names
summary: The two New York street heroes have known each other's identities since the 1980s and act as each other's confessors; Matt has been Peter's lawyer.

events.note: First meeting.
Mutual identities openly acknowledged.

label: The argument nobody wins
summary: Matt arrests, Frank kills; every meeting is the same argument. Garth Ennis's Punisher vol. 4 #3 (2000) — Frank tying Matt up with a gun — is the definitive version.

events.note: First clash.
'The Choice'.

label: Introduced to kill him
summary: The Punisher debuted hired to kill Spider-Man, and their relationship has been Peter's refusal to accept Frank ever since.

events.note: Punisher debuts hunting Spider-Man.

label: The most stable marriage at Marvel
summary: Began as a one-night stand in Alias #1, became a pregnancy, a marriage (New Avengers Annual #1, 2006) and a daughter. Written consistently as two damaged adults who chose each other.

events.note: They meet.
Wedding.
Danielle Cage is born.

label: Registration's loudest objector
summary: Luke refused to register in Civil War and led the underground New Avengers against Tony's side; he never fully forgave the Stark who sent Cape-Killers to his door.

events.note: Luke refuses registration at midnight.

label: She sat behind him in high school
summary: Alias retconned Jessica into Midtown High as the girl with a crush on Peter Parker; they became Avengers teammates decades later.

events.note: Jessica's origin, with Peter in her class.

label: Cap handed him the team
summary: Steve asked Luke to lead the New Avengers after Siege (2010); Luke's ambivalence about Cap's establishment and his loyalty to the man personally is the Heroic Age in one relationship.

events.note: Luke leads the New Avengers at Cap's request.

label: Defenders
summary: Strange, Hulk and Namor as the original 'non-team'; the Hulk's exile by the Illuminati (with Strange a member) broke the trust.

events.note: The Defenders form.
Hulk breaks Strange's hands.

label: Defenders and Illuminati
summary: Allies in two secret societies; Namor's walkout from the Illuminati over the Hulk, and his return to it for the incursions, map the character's whole relationship with the surface.

events.note: Defenders.
The Illuminati revealed.

label: Illuminati
summary: Strange and Stark, with Reed, Xavier, Namor and Black Bolt, ran the universe in secret; Strange was the member most troubled by it.

events.note: The Illuminati revealed.
Strange rejoins for the incursions.

label: Illuminati
summary: Two of Marvel's great patriarchs, both in the Illuminati, both guilty of the same sin of deciding for everyone.

events.note: First X-Men/FF crossover.
Both members.

label: Father to a man older than himself
summary: Cable is Scott's son by Madelyne Pryor, sent to the future as an infant to survive a techno-organic virus and returned as a grizzled soldier. Scott's guilt and Nathan's distance thawed in the Askani'son stories and froze again on Krakoa, where a teenage Cable displaced the older one.

events.note: Baby Nathan sent to the future.
Cable attends Scott and Jean's wedding.
Scott and Jean raise Nathan in the future.

label: The stepmother who raised him
summary: Jean is not Cable's biological mother (that was her clone Madelyne) but she and Scott raised him for twelve years in the future.

events.note: Raising Nathan as 'Redd' and 'Slym'.

label: The odd couple
summary: Deadpool debuted as a mercenary hired against Cable; Cable & Deadpool (2004–08) made them Marvel's definitive mismatched partners — the soldier with a plan and the lunatic who ruins it.

events.note: Deadpool's first appearance.
Teleport-bonded together.
Series ends with the partnership intact.

label: He wants to be friends; Logan doesn't
summary: Deadpool's one-sided fixation on Wolverine as a peer (both Weapon X, both healing factors) and Logan's contempt is a thirty-year joke that occasionally turns serious.

events.note: First fight.
Deadpool hired to kill Wolverine.

label: Reluctant best friends
summary: Spider-Man/Deadpool (2016–19) wrote Wade's hero-worship of Peter as the thing that might make him better, and Peter's refusal to indulge it as the thing that might not.

events.note: Series begins.

label: Two philosophies of mutant supremacy
summary: Apocalypse's survival-of-the-fittest and Magneto's protectionism are opposed readings of the same premise; in the Age of Apocalypse, Magneto leads the resistance against him. On Krakoa they sat on the same council.

events.note: Age of Apocalypse: Magneto's X-Men vs. Apocalypse.
Both seated on the Quiet Council.

label: The dream vs. the strong
summary: Apocalypse is the only major villain whose vision is a direct refutation of Xavier's; in the Age of Apocalypse, Xavier's death is what lets him win. Krakoa put them in the same room.

events.note: Xavier's death creates the Age of Apocalypse.
Apocalypse on Xavier's council.

label: The second protégée
summary: Jubilee pulled Logan off a crucifix in the Australian outback and followed him for years; she is the Claremont-era successor to Kitty in his life, and later the one who, as a vampire, he refused to give up on.

events.note: Jubilee rescues the crucified Wolverine.
Logan helps the vampire Jubilee.

label: The clone he raised as a daughter
summary: Laura was made from Logan's DNA and trained as a weapon; he took her in (New X-Men, 2006), she took his name after his death. Written explicitly as father and daughter, by both.

events.note: Laura's origin.
'You're my daughter'.
Laura becomes Wolverine.

label: Logan's two kids
summary: Kitty and Jubilee are the two teenagers Wolverine raised, a generation apart; they compare notes.

events.note: Jubilee in the role Kitty once had, with Kitty in Excalibur.

label: The time-displaced Jean and the clone
summary: The young, displaced Jean Grey was the first X-Man to treat Laura as a person rather than a weapon.

events.note: Laura joins the time-displaced X-Men.

label: Former spouses, heads of state
summary: After the annulment, as Regent of Arakko and King of Wakanda, they deal with each other as sovereigns.

events.note: Storm rules Arakko on Mars.

label: Two cosmic scales
summary: Thanos has fought and manipulated Galactus repeatedly (Infinity Gauntlet, Thanos vol. 1); neither regards the other as a peer.

events.note: Galactus among the cosmic beings Thanos defeats.
Thanos helps Galactus against Hunger.

label: Infinity-era enemies
summary: Carol has fought Thanos in every Infinity-scale crossover since 1991 and in Infinity Wars (2018).

events.note: Thanos erases half the universe; Carol among the survivors.
Thanos's death at Gamora's hands.

label: Doom in the armour
summary: Doom's Camelot team-up with Tony (1981) became, in Infamous Iron Man (2016–17), Doom taking up Iron Man's identity while Tony was comatose — a rivalry that curdled into stewardship.

events.note: Doomquest: Doom and Stark stranded in Camelot.
Doom becomes Iron Man.

label: Avengers together
summary: Hank McCoy's Avengers years (1975–79) were the loosest, happiest version of the character, and Jan was his closest friend on the team.

events.note: Beast joins the Avengers.

label: Wartime comrades, Avengers teammates
summary: They fought together in 1941 (Uncanny X-Men #268); Cap sponsored Logan's Avengers membership in 2005 and asked him to run the X-Men's school in Schism.

events.note: Cap, Logan and the Black Widow in 1941 Madripoor.
Cap recruits Wolverine to the Avengers.

label: The other strength contest
summary: Marvel's first hero-vs-hero fight; it recurs every decade and ends in a draw every time, by editorial law.

events.note: The first fight.
The rematch, with the Avengers.

label: The Iron Spider
summary: Tony made Peter a suit and a protégé before Civil War and lost him when Peter unmasked for registration and then defected; the betrayal ran both ways.

events.note: The Iron Spider armour.
Peter unmasks on television.
Peter switches sides.

label: The hero he wanted to be
summary: Peter's decision to follow Cap in Civil War was written as a son choosing a father; Steve's 'plant yourself like a tree' speech in Amazing Spider-Man #537 (2007) is the relationship's thesis.

events.note: Cap's speech to Peter about standing your ground.

label: The god who respects him
summary: Thor regards Steve as the one mortal whose worthiness is not in question; Cap has lifted Mjolnir (Thor #390, 1988; Fear Itself, 2011).

events.note: Cap lifts Mjolnir.
Cap wields the hammer against the Serpent.

label: Chairwoman and soldier
summary: Jan was the Avengers' chairwoman through the Bronze Age with Cap as her field commander; a working relationship written with real affection.

events.note: Jan becomes chairwoman.

label: Cap's kooky quartet
summary: The three ex-villains Cap took in in 1965 — Clint, Wanda, Pietro — were a unit; Clint's loyalty to Wanda survived Disassembled, in which she killed him.

events.note: 'Cap's Kooky Quartet'.
Wanda's breakdown kills Hawkeye.
Clint restored.

label: Ultimate: briefly consummated
summary: In the Ultimate universe, Jean actually left Scott for Logan — the thing the 616 version never allows.

events.note: Jean and Logan.

label: Ultimate: Reed became the villain
summary: The Ultimate universe inverted the pairing: Reed Richards became the Maker, a genocidal super-scientist, and Doom was killed by Ben Grimm.

events.note: Ultimate Doom debuts.
Ben Grimm kills Doom.
Reed as the Maker.
